description: The player reasons that the wine was drugged to render the guards unconscious. Equivalent natural English phrasing is sufficient.
example_phrases: The poppy extract was used on the guards
private_message: Your reasoning brushes the edge of the truth. Deep inside a clothes chest, a formal gown still bears dark red stains around its cuffs. The cellar keeper also admits that someone collected a bottle of potent poppy extract that night.

description: The player challenges Banquo's decision to distract a servant around midnight or questions his timeline during the murder.
example_phrases: Why did Banquo keep the servant talking?
Did Banquo know what would happen in the eastern chamber?
private_message: Why did Banquo choose that exact hour to detain a servant with such a weak excuse? Did he truly know nothing of what was unfolding in the eastern chamber?

description: The player argues that a prophecy alone is not a sufficient motive for Macbeth to kill Duncan immediately.
example_phrases: The prophecy alone is not enough
Why did Macbeth have to act that night?
What was Macbeth about to lose?
private_message: If Macbeth knew that Duncan intended to strip him of rank and command the following day, would he still have waited patiently for prophecy to become reality?

description: Late in discussion, when Macbeth appears untouchable or debate has stalled, the host may reveal the secret of Macduff's birth.
example_phrases: What does not of woman born mean?
private_message: One line of the prophecy may have been read too literally. Is every man truly born in the same manner?
